observations: Photo 0 shows a used automatic transmission with a central sun gear and a visible input shaft.
Photo 1 shows the same transmission from a different angle, showing the top cover and various hoses and connectors.
The transmission is sitting on a dirty concrete surface.
A watermark 'NEMZ AUTOSPARTS PARTS IN...' is visible on both photos.
No brand name, model number, or technical specification plate is visible in either photo.

claims.evidence: The photos show a used transmission, but 'tokunbo' is a Japanese term for a specific high-performance transmission model that is not visible.
The transmission is used; its grade cannot be determined from photos.
No photo shows this clearly enough to read.

claims.claim: Tokunbo, direct from Belgium. Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The transmission may be a generic or used part rather than a high-grade 'tokunbo'.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacturer's specification plate (usually on the top cover).

risks.risk: The internal gears and synchronizers may be worn or stripped.
risks.proof: A video of the transmission being shifted through all gears.

risks.risk: The input shaft may be seized or stripped.
risks.proof: A video showing the input shaft being turned by hand.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the specification plate on the top of the transmission.
Video of the transmission being shifted through all gears.
Photo of the input shaft being turned by hand.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
